mainTopic: How רבי's four nights of דם בתולים are counted, a story about misapplying רב's ruling, and how long an עונה שלמה is for a girl who already saw blood.
overview: The גמרא tries to explain an earlier case where רבי gave a newly married girl four nights, spread over twelve months, in which her blood was blamed on the torn hymen and not treated as נדה blood. It tests and rejects several timings: all four nights as a minor, all four as a נערה (שמואל says נערות lasts exactly six months), two and two (רב counts all relations during minority as one night), and one-two-one. The final answer is one night for her minor years and three during נערות, with each period counted as two months. Next comes a story: מנימין סקסנאה planned to apply רב's lenient first-night ruling even to a woman who had already seen blood, but he died on the road, and שמואל said about רב, 'No mishap shall befall the righteous.' After a side teaching from רב about losing one's teeth, the גמרא returns to the משנה. A ברייתא says that a girl who saw blood in her father's house gets an עונה שלמה, which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל defines as a night and half a day. The גמרא then asks whether that much time is really needed, and begins a contrasting ברייתא about purifying winepresses that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The minor option fails: the משנה gives more than four nights
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that all four nights were given while she was a minor. For a girl that young, the משנה gives her 'until the wound heals'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'until the wound heals'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is knocking down a suggestion about how רבי gave the girl her four nights. It quotes the words of the משנה to show the suggestion cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose all four nights were given while she was still a קטנה, before her time to see blood. Our משנה (following בית הלל) gives such a girl 'until the wound heals', which can be much longer than four nights. So a four-night limit cannot be talking about her time as a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: Until the wound heals; the time a young bride gets to blame blood on the torn hymen.

phrases.english: 'Until the wound heals' we learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the rejection of the option, raised just before this section, that all four nights were given during her time as a minor.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that all four nights fell during her years as a minor.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A minor gets 'until the wound heals', not a fixed four nights.

steps.title: New suggestion: all four nights were in her young-woman stage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי gave her all four nights while she was a נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he gave her all of them during her days as a young woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to explain רבי's ruling. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the minor stage did not work, maybe all four nights came during the נערות stage. A girl at that stage gets exactly four nights, so this seems to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The stage of a young woman, after she shows signs of maturity and before full adulthood.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ כּוּלְּהוּ בִּימֵי נַעֲרוּת —
phrases.english: Rather, that he gave her all of them during the days of young-womanhood —
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all four nights.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ כּוּלְּהוּ בִּימֵי נַעֲרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected minor option with a new timing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four nights were given while she was a minor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The four nights were all given while she was a נערה.

steps.title: There is no twelve-month young-woman stage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion using שמואל, who says נערות lasts only six months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there such a thing as twelve months of נערות? But שמואל said: between נערות and בגרות there are only six months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new suggestion. The four nights were spread over twelve months, but the נערות stage is too short for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's ruling covered twelve months. According to שמואל, a girl moves from נערה to בוגרת after just six months. So all twelve months cannot fall inside the נערות stage.

keyTerms.meaning: Full adulthood; the stage of a בּוֹגֶרֶת.
Is there? (a question that expects the answer 'no').

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲרוּת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ מִי אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: Is there a young-woman stage of twelve months?
But didn't Shmuel say:
There is nothing between young-womanhood and full adulthood
except six months only!

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲרוּת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ מִי אִיכָּא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all four nights, spread over twelve months, fell during נערות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל fixes נערות at six months, which is too short to hold twelve months.

steps.title: Maybe שמואל only meant 'at least six months'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers reading שמואל as giving a minimum: no less than six months, but possibly more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: it is less than this that does not exist, but more does exist—
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the suggestion by reading שמואל's six months as a minimum. This sets up the next step, which rejects that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If six months is only the shortest possible נערות, then some girls could be נערות for twelve months. That would allow רבי's twelve months to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible defense).

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵימָא בְּצִיר מֵהָכִי הוּא דְּלֵיכָּא,
phrases.english: And if you say: it is less than this that does not exist,
but more does exist —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא בְּצִיר מֵהָכִי הוּא דְּלֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to defend step 2 against step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's six months is a fixed length.
steps.terutzMaskana: Six months is only a minimum.

steps.title: The word 'only' rules out a longer stage
steps.stepSummary: שמואל said 'only', so six months is exact and cannot be longer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense by pointing to שמואל's own word 'only'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בלבד shows that six months is the exact length, not a minimum. So the all-נערות suggestion falls.

phrases.english: But he said 'only'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Reading שמואל as giving a minimum, and with it the all-נערות suggestion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'only' makes six months exact.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, נערות lasts exactly six months, so twelve months cannot all fall in that stage.

steps.title: New suggestion: two nights as a minor, two as a young woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי split the nights: two while she was a minor and two while she was a נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he gave her two during her days as a minor and two during her days as a young woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third way to explain the case. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting the nights across the two stages would let the twelve months stretch past the six-month נערות stage. Neither stage would have to hold all four nights.

keyTerms.meaning: Minority; the time before a girl shows signs of maturity.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ שְׁתַּיִם בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת
phrases.english: Rather, that he gave her two during the days of minority
and two during the days of young-womanhood,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ שְׁתַּיִם בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four nights came during נערות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two nights came during minority and two during נערות.

steps.title: Challenge from רב חיננא בר שלמיא's question to רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up a question asked of רב about a girl whose time to see blood arrived while she was already married.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חיננא בר שלמיא asked רב: if her time to see blood arrived while she was married, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to the split suggestion by quoting a question asked of רב. His answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about a girl who married as a minor and then reached the age of seeing blood. How are her four nights counted? רב's answer will decide whether nights during minority can count as separate nights.

keyTerms.meaning: Her time to see (menstrual blood) arrived.
Under her husband; while she is married to him.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מֵרַב:
phrases.english: But Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelamya asked Rav:

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת תַּחַת בַּעְלָהּ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If her time to see arrived while under her husband, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מֵרַב
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion of two nights as a minor and two as a נערה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's ruling about this case will show that nights during minority cannot count as two separate nights.

steps.title: רב: all relations as a minor count as just one night
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that all the relations during her minority count as one. She gets only three more nights to complete four.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: all the relations you have are only one, and the rest complete the four nights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question, and this completes the challenge against the split suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: However many times the husband had relations while she was a minor, it all counts as a single night. After her time arrives, she gets three more nights to reach four. So רבי could not have given her two separate nights during her minority.

phrases.english: He said to him:
All the acts of relations that you have —
phrases.notes: He means the relations during the time she was still a minor.

phrases.english: are only one,
and the rest complete the four nights.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כׇּל בְּעִילוֹת שֶׁאַתָּה בּוֹעֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7, which completes the challenge to step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the four nights are counted for a girl who married as a minor and whose time to see blood arrived later.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All relations during minority count as one night, and three more nights complete the four.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the husband gets only one act of relations. He is saying that all of them together count as just one of the four nights.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling blocks the idea that two separate nights could be given during minority, so the split suggestion is in trouble.

steps.title: A new split: one, two, and one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי gave one night during קטנות, two during נערות, and one during בגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say that he gave her one night while she was a minor, two while she was a נערה, and one while she was a grown woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to count the four nights so it fits שמואל's six months of נערות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since נערות is exactly six months, the גמרא spreads the four nights across three life stages. Only two of them fall during נערות, and the fourth falls after she became a בוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when a girl is a minor (קטנה)
The roughly six-month stage of being a נערה, a young woman
The stage of being a fully grown woman (בוגרת)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ אַחַת בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת,
phrases.english: Rather, that he gave her one night during her days as a minor,
and two nights during her days as a young woman,
and one night during her days as a grown woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ אַחַת בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier split now that רב counts all the minor-years relations as one night
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-dividing the four nights across three stages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four nights had to fit inside קטנות and נערות
steps.terutzMaskana: One night may have fallen in בגרות, so נערות needs only two

steps.title: Does a regular grown woman get more than one night?
steps.stepSummary: The new split only works if a normal בוגרת gets more than one night. If she does not, רבי should have given her only the בעילת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if a regular grown woman gets more than one night. Then just as her minor years took one night off her נערות, her נערות took one night off her בגרות, leaving one. But if a regular grown woman gets no more than one night, he should have given her only the first act of relations and nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the one-two-one suggestion. It shows that the suggestion depends on how many nights a normal בוגרת gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is that each earlier stage takes one night away from the next stage. If a normal בוגרת gets more than one night, taking one away still leaves a night, which fits. But if a normal בוגרת gets only one night, taking one away should leave her with just the single act of בעילת מצוה, not a full night.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say: it fits one possibility, but not the other
The first act of relations that completes the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not deciding here how many nights a בוגרת gets. It only shows that the one-two-one idea works with one answer and fails with the other.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that we generally give a grown woman more,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאַהֲנַי קַטְנוּת בִּימֵי נַעֲרוּת
phrases.english: then just as her minority took effect on her days as a young woman
to take one away from her,
so too her young-woman stage takes effect on her grown-woman stage
to take one away from her.
But if you say

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹגֶרֶת דְּעָלְמָא לָא יָהֲבִינַן לַהּ טְפֵי
phrases.english: that we do not give a regular grown woman more,

phrases.aramaic: לָא לִיתֵּב לַהּ אֶלָּא בְּעִילַת מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: he should have given her only the relations of the מצוה,
and nothing more!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בּוֹגֶרֶת בְּעָלְמָא יָהֲבִינַן לַהּ טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the one-two-one suggestion of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that one of the four nights fell during בגרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each stage takes one night off the next, a בוגרת who normally gets only one night should end up with just the בעילת מצוה, not a full night

steps.title: One night as a minor, three as a נערה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי gave one night during קטנות and three during נערות, because each עונה was two months, not three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he gave her one night while she was a minor and three while she was a נערה. Do you think each period was three months? No, each period was two months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the בגרות idea and fits all three remaining nights inside the six months of נערות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that six months seemed to hold only two periods of three months each. The גמרא says each period was two months, so six months hold three. That fits both שמואל's exact six months and רב's rule that the minor years count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: introduces the correct explanation
Do you think? It introduces an assumption the גמרא is about to reject
A period, one stretch of time counted as one night

steps.whatToRemember: Final count for רבי's case: one night (all the minor years together) plus three nights during the six months of נערות, at one per two months. Four in total.

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם, דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ אַחַת בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת
phrases.english: Actually, he gave her one night during her days as a minor
and three nights during her days as a young woman.
Do you think that every three months
was one period?
Every two months was one period.
phrases.notes: So the six months of נערות hold three periods, which means three nights.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם, דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ אַחַת בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת וְשָׁלֹשׁ בִּימֵי נַעֲרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10 by dropping the בגרות night
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting a hidden assumption about how long each period was
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each period was three months, so six months of נערות hold only two nights
steps.terutzMaskana: Each period was two months, so three nights fit inside נערות

steps.title: מנימין סקסנאה wants to rule like רב
steps.stepSummary: מנימין סקסנאה, on his way to שמואל's place, planned to rule like רב even for a woman who had already seen blood, thinking רב makes no distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: מנימין סקסנאה was walking to שמואל's place. He planned to act in practice like רב, even if the woman had already seen blood. He said: רב does not distinguish between a woman who saw and one who did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a sage who wanted to apply רב's lenient rule in a practical case. It is setting up what happens next in the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנימין assumed that רב's ruling, which lets a grown woman treat the bleeding as דם בתולים for the whole first night, applies even if she had already seen menstrual blood before marriage. He was ready to act on this in שמואל's own place.

keyTerms.meaning: To act in practice, to give a real ruling

phrases.english: Minyamin Saksana
was going along to the place of Shmuel;
he thought to act in practice in line with Rav,
even if she had seen.
He said: Rav does not distinguish
between a woman who saw and a woman who did not see.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְיָמִין סַקְסְנָאָה הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל לְאַתְרֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי's case to a story about applying רב's ruling in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנימין understood רב to allow the whole first night as דם בתולים even for a woman who had already seen blood

steps.title: מנימין dies before ruling, and שמואל praises רב
steps.stepSummary: מנימין סקסנאה died on the road before he could rule wrongly in רב's name. שמואל applied the פסוק 'No mishap shall befall the righteous' to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before he got there, he died on the road. שמואל said about רב: 'No mishap shall befall the righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story from the previous step. מנימין never got to give his mistaken ruling, because he died on the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנימין wanted to stretch רב's ruling to a case רב did not mean. His death stopped a wrong ruling from going out in רב's name. שמואל read this as Heaven guarding a צדיק from having a mistake attached to his words.

keyTerms.meaning: No mishap shall befall the righteous (משלי 12:21)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling that a grown woman gets the whole first night was not meant for a woman who had already seen menstrual blood. מנימין's plan to rule that way was a mistake, and it never happened.

phrases.english: Before [he arrived], he died on the road,
phrases.notes: "He" is מנימין סקסנאה from the last step. He never reached שמואל's place to give his ruling.

phrases.english: Shmuel recited about Rav
"No mishap shall befall the righteous."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in step 12. The mistaken ruling was never carried out.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wrong extension of רב's ruling never became practice. שמואל sees this as Heaven protecting רב.

steps.title: When teeth fall out, food decreases
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר שלמיא quotes רב: once a person loses his teeth, his food decreases. He learns this from a פסוק in עמוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר שלמיא said in רב's name: once a person's teeth fall out, his food becomes less, as it says, 'I have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side teaching, an אגדה, from רב. It is not part of the topic of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'clean teeth' right next to 'lack of bread.' רב reads 'clean teeth' as having no teeth at all, so a person who cannot chew ends up eating less.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleanness of teeth, read here as having no teeth

steps.confusionAlert: This is a side teaching. Do not try to connect it to the laws of the girl's bleeding. The גמרא goes back to the משנה in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chinnana bar Shelamya said in the name of Rav:
Once a person's teeth fall out,
his food becomes less,
as it is stated:
"And I also have given you
cleanness of teeth in all your cities,
phrases.notes: עמוס 4:6. "Clean teeth" here means having no teeth at all.

phrases.english: and lack of bread in all your places."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching that steps away from the halachic discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Losing one's teeth leads to eating less, learned from עמוס 4:6.

steps.title: A girl who saw blood in her father's house gets a full period
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and brings a ברייתא. In the ברייתא, בית הלל say that a girl who already saw blood before marriage has the whole night, and she is given an עונה שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'She saw and was still.' The ברייתא teaches: if she saw blood while still in her father's house, בית הלל say the whole night is hers, and she is given a complete period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a girl who saw menstrual blood before her wedding. It brings a ברייתא with בית הלל's ruling for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This girl had already seen menstrual blood while still in her father's house, before her wedding. Even so, בית הלל give her one full period of time in which bleeding is blamed on the torn hymen and not on her period. The next step defines how long that period is.

keyTerms.meaning: She saw blood while still in her father's house, before marriage

phrases.english: "She saw and was still."
The Rabbis taught:
If she saw blood while still in her father's house,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה שֶׁלָּהּ,
phrases.english: Beit Hillel say: the whole night is hers,
and they give her a complete period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side teachings, the גמרא goes back to the משנה and its case of a girl who already saw blood in her father's house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who saw blood in her father's house is given an עונה שלמה, during which bleeding is blamed on the first relations.

steps.title: A complete period is a night and half a day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how long an עונה שלמה is. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers: a night and half a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long is a complete period? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explained: a night and half a day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defines exactly how much time 'a complete period' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה שלמה is more than just the night. It also covers half of the next day. This exact length is what the גמרא challenges in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A night and half a day

phrases.english: And how long is a complete period?
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel explained:
A night and half a day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term עונה שלמה used in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long an עונה שלמה is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A night and half a day, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Do we really need that much time? A contrast from winepresses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether an עונה really has to be that long. It begins a contrasting ברייתא about someone who wants to purify his impure winepresses and olive presses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really need all that? They contrasted it with a ברייתא: if someone's winepresses and olive presses were impure and he wanted to use them in purity, what does he do? The planks, the palm branches and the troughs, he rinses them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the length 'a night and half a day.' It starts quoting another ברייתא that seems to use a shorter amount of time, and that ברייתא continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'do we need all this?' tells us the גמרא expects an עונה to be shorter. The winepress ברייתא is brought because it will use the same idea of a set time period. Here it has only reached the first instruction: rinse the planks, branches and troughs.

keyTerms.meaning: But do we really need all this?

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not finished here. The ברייתא keeps going, and the part about the length of time comes later.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's definition of an עונה שלמה as a night and half a day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא about purifying presses seems to treat an עונה as a shorter time. So why should an עונה here need a full night and half a day?
